rationale:
Evidence: iteration 4 is the best raced design (81.56). Its sensors were at x = -0.045, -0.0225, 0, 0.0225, 0.045 with y = 0.05, kp 7.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.4 and last_direction. It scored 135.7 on the oval (progress 0.33), 67.9 on the s-bend (progress 0.17) and 41.1 on the slalom (progress 0.10). All 60 trials ended off track, max_error was 0.063 m on each track, and there was about one line loss per run.

Correction: the authorised entity1 rationale says iteration 4 had x = ±0.06. The outcome table and the iteration-4 design both show ±0.045, so I use ±0.045 as the baseline. The ±0.06 layout was never raced, and the outer-sensor engagement figure was taken from the wrong baseline.

Review of the round-2 critique. I accept point 1: moving the row forward raises the effective heading gain (about 40 percent at y = 0.07 against 0.05), so steering_oscillation may rise, and I keep the oscillation kill rule. I accept point 2: forward position does not widen lateral reach, so I do not claim that line_loss_events will fall for geometric reasons. I accept point 5 and the completion concern as open issues, but I do not change speed in this race. I reject the critique's suggestion to fall back to x = ±0.06 now. That layout cuts the near-centre slope by about 2.5 times and was never validated, so it would confound this test. I also reject any kp change, because the kp evidence is confounded and any change would be a second variable.

Change: one variable from iteration 4. The sensor row moves from y = 0.05 to y = 0.07, with x, sensor size, controller and body all unchanged. The aim is earlier steering reaction at bends, where the excursions occur. The test isolates forward lookahead on the best-raced layout. Engagement at x = 0.045 reaches roughly 0.065 m offset, which covers the band where the peaks sit.

Hypotheses: max_error falls below 0.0629 m on at least two tracks; progress on the oval stays at or above 0.33; line_loss_events are 1 or fewer per run. These are predictions, not derived values. Kill rule: if steering_oscillation rises by more than 30 percent, or max_error gets worse on two or more tracks, revert to y = 0.05 and do not raise kd. Completion at base_speed 1.4 remains untested, so completion_time is requested. If runs stay on track with completion_time above 3 s, the next single test is base_speed plus 0.1.
